AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To investigate whether lactotripeptides (LTP) supplementations alleviate the decrease in the maximal isometric force (MIF), an indirect marker of muscle damage, following eccentric exercise (ECC).

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Twenty-two young men performed 50-ECC of the elbow flexors using an isokinetic dynamometer. The subjects were randomly assigned to either the placebo or LTP group, and were each given a 4.5 mg/day placebo or LTP three-time on the exercise day and the day after. MIF and brachial arterial diameter were assessed before and two days after the ECC.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The interaction of time and group on MIF was significant (p < 0.05); MIF was significantly decreased in both groups following ECC (p < 0.005). The interaction of brachial arterial diameter was significant (p < 0.05); brachial arterial diameter was significantly increased in only the LTP group (p < 0.005). In addition, the change in MIF was significantly related to the change in brachial arterial diameter after adjusting for body weight and change in ROM (p < 0.05).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The present results suggest that LTP supplementation alleviates the decrease in the MIF via an increase in brachial arterial diameter following ECC.
